title: Indefinite Integrals and the Substitution Method
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: The Substitution Rule for Integrals
definitions.latex: \int f(g(x)) g'(x) dx = \int f(u) du, \quad \text{where } u = g(x), \; du = g'(x) dx
definitions.statement: If u = g(x) is a differentiable function whose range is an interval I and f is continuous on I, then substitution transforms an integral into a simpler form by reversing the Chain Rule of differentiation.
conditions: f is continuous on range of g
definitions.explanation: The differential du = g'(x) dx replaces g'(x) dx entirely, simplifying the integration.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Substitution is the integral calculus analog of the Chain Rule.

definitions.title: Generalized Power Rule for Integration
definitions.statement: Direct integration formula when the integrand contains an expression raised to a power multiplied by its derivative.
definitions.explanation: Setting u = g(x) immediately yields int u^n du = u^(n+1)/(n+1) + C.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Enables instant integration of composite power terms.
